item.text: {"0":"Across all four datasets, reduce only the tied real-item embedding normalization multiplier from 0.75 to 0.70, preserving the vocabulary-dependent radius formula and raw learned exclusive mask vector. The regression at 0.80 motivates testing weaker item magnitude relative to positional inputs. Preserve features, dimensions, backbone, history, scoring, loss and optimizer; use the same normalization in training and prediction, with one model per category.","1":"Across all four datasets, replace standardized log-frequency modulation with training-item frequency percentile modulation: scale real-item inputs by 1 + 0.02*(2*p-1), where p is the midrank percentile of each item's training count across the real-item vocabulary. This tests a bounded frequency feature less sensitive to count outliers. Keep padding and mask scales at 1, store scales in each checkpoint, and preserve learned embeddings, topology, readout, loss and optimizer. Retain one model per category.","2":"Across all four datasets, add label smoothing of 0.02 to the existing masked-item cross-entropy over real-item classes, retaining temperature 0.8 and uniform masked-target averaging. Mild smoothing may reduce overconfidence without the stronger temperature or recency-weighting changes that regressed. Preserve features, embeddings, backbone, scoring, optimizer, sampling, scheduler and batch/epoch settings. Retain one model per category and unchanged appended-mask inference.","3":"Across all four datasets, replace forward ordinal position IDs with reverse ordinal IDs over nonpadding tokens: the rightmost token receives position 1, its predecessor 2, and padding 0. This anchors positions to recency across variable-length histories and gives the appended prediction mask position 1. Apply the same rule during masked-target training and prediction. Preserve position-table dimensions, observed-history truncation, embeddings, bidirectional backbone, masked-state readout, scoring, loss and optimizer; retain one model per category."}
